conventions.convention: P-Glivenko–Cantelli means uniform convergence in probability; strongly P-Glivenko–Cantelli means uniform convergence almost surely. Pointwise measurability requires a countable subclass providing pointwise sequential approximations.
Envelopes dominate each function P-almost surely. Countable pointwise approximation supplies the common samplewise control needed for uniform statements.

The canonical pseudometric is ρP(f,g) = {P[(f−g)−P(f−g)]²}^(1/2); zero distance permits differences that are constant almost surely. Equicontinuity uses outer probability and pairs with distance strictly below δ.
Donsker convergence is convergence of outer expectations against every bounded uniformly continuous real functional on ℓ∞(F), to a tight Borel centered Gaussian law with covariance P[(f−Pf)(g−Pg)].
The bracketing Glivenko–Cantelli theorem has a choice-free convergence-in-probability branch and a strong branch explicitly assuming Countable Choice.
The equicontinuity lemma assumes Countable Choice and positive finite envelope L² norm; the functional CLT assumes AC and treats zero envelope norm separately.
Dudley's covering numbers use closed balls with centers in the index space. A specified listed countable dense subset provides process separability; diameter zero is included.
The local maximal inequality concerns a countable class and a supremum, with nested finite partitions, actual pointwise cell oscillations, supplied representatives, and dyadic L² oscillation bounds.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let Xi be iid with law P, and let F be a nonempty pointwise-measurable class of measurable functions with a nonnegative envelope F satisfying 0 < ‖F‖P,2 < ∞. If the integral from 0 to 1 of sqrt(log N[](ε‖F‖P,2,F,L²(P))) dε is finite, then Gn is asymptotically equicontinuous in probability with respect to ρP.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For iid observations with law P and a nonempty pointwise-measurable class of measurable real functions with measurable envelope F ≥ 0 and PF² < ∞, the empirical process is zero almost surely when ‖F‖P,2 = 0. Otherwise, finiteness of the normalized L²(P) bracketing square-root entropy integral on (0,1) implies that the class is P-Donsker, with tight centered Gaussian bridge covariance K(f,g) = P[(f−Pf)(g−Pg)].

Let Xi be iid with law P, and let F be a nonempty pointwise-measurable class of measurable real functions with a nonnegative integrable envelope. If N[](ε,F,L¹(P)) < ∞ for every ε > 0, then supf |Pnf−Pf| tends to zero in probability. If Countable Choice is assumed, this convergence is almost sure.

For a real process on a nonempty totally bounded pseudometric space (T,d), with the specified countable separability and centered increments satisfying E exp(λ(Xs−Xt)) ≤ exp(λ²d(s,t)²/2) for every s,t and real λ, finiteness of the covering square-root entropy integral from 0 to the diameter D implies E supt |Xt−Xt0| ≤ C times that integral for every t0 ∈ T. If D = 0, the integral and supremum are zero.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page and empirical-process and entropy definitions against their actual uses. Empirical scaling, countable and outer conventions, class-internal closed covering balls, and almost-everywhere measurable brackets are preserved.

Checked the centered sub-Gaussian definition and Bernstein statement and proof. Dudley uses the all-real-parameter MGF condition; the bracketing maximal proof centers bounded functions, uses absolute bound 2b, and bounds their variances by their second moments.

The asymptotic-distribution definition is used only for finite-dimensional weak convergence. The functional CLT separately establishes Gaussian tightness, empirical equicontinuity, and outer-expectation process convergence.

Checked the downstream page and both consistency theorems. The page retains pointwise measurability, integrable envelopes, and finite L¹ bracketing at every positive scale; it invokes the choice-free probability branch. The fixed-dimensional Z reduction uses a finite coordinate bound and retains explicit measurability assumptions.
